data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The RFC 9110 distinction is HTTP-semantics-local and does not transfer cleanly to event-log writer semantics. The append-only log does not require 'safe' or 'idempotent' in the RFC sense at all; it requires a stronger, log-specific property: deterministic-replay idempotence, where the replay of a sequence of operations reproduces the same final state regardless of delivery multiplicity, which is neither pure safety nor pure idempotence.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If RFC 9110's definition of idempotence is broad enough to cover sequences (it is per-method), this candidate is wrong and the standard view holds.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the log's correctness proof only needs per-operation idempotence (not sequence-level), the stronger property is unnecessary.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"RFC 9110 defines idempotence per-method: 'several identical requests have the same effect as one.' But an event log operates on sequences with causality (ordering, dependencies). The required property is that the composition of retried appends is equivalent to a single canonical sequence \u2014 a property of the aggregate, not of individual operations. The mechanism is content-addressing or operation-ID deduplication over the entire write history, which subsumes per-operation idempotence. Calling it 'idempotent' (RFC sense) is a useful approximation but technically conflates per-method semantics with sequence semantics.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
